title: The Casino of Lost Tuesdays
premise: A slot machine pays out in memories of work shifts never worked.
pressure: A casino slot machine is paying out memories of Tuesdays you never worked. The attendant recognizes the uniform in one vision but not the coworker beside you. A guest is demanding compensation for a shift they insist they already played.
investigate: Compare the payout log with schedules before treating remembered work as owed wages
success: The log holds a real transaction number against an impossible Tuesday. The supervisor preserves it for review without charging either employee.
failure: The machine resets before you get a printout. The attendant records the guest's account while the security clock supplies a second timestamp.
help: Help the attendant close the malfunctioning machine and give the guest a fair complaint route
helpOutcome: The machine is tagged out, the guest gets a receipt, and nobody is asked to prove a memory to keep their job. The slot display flashes TAKE YOUR BREAK.

title: The Bridge from the Other Side
premise: A stranger remembers crossing a bridge that was demolished before their birth.
pressure: A traveler describes crossing a bridge that collapsed before he was born. His photograph shows its decking, a driverless car and a handwritten sign reading SLOW. He knows which family member took the picture, but not why she never mentioned the bridge.
investigate: Reconstruct the route from his account without treating memory as a crime
success: Fresh tool marks appear on the far bank where no bridge has stood for years. You photograph them beside a current survey marker, without naming their maker.
failure: The photograph fogs. He remembers the river bend and his aunt's laugh. You write down both rather than invent a date.
help: Walk with him across the present-day crossing and let him keep his story
helpOutcome: He reaches home safely. His impossible childhood can remain his, even if the bridge turns out to belong to nobody's map.

title: The Banjo that Predicts Lightning
premise: A musician plays weather forecasts as bluegrass solos.
pressure: A bluegrass musician can forecast storms by picking a banjo solo, but the county weather report has no rain in it. The fiddler wants to keep playing; an elderly neighbor wants someone to check the culvert before dark.
investigate: Record the melody, then cross-check the road and pressure readings
success: The refrain repeats the name of a low road, note for letter, as water starts pooling under the bridge. The crew blocks the crossing before the rain arrives.
failure: A string breaks halfway through. The musician can't remember the last bar, but the neighbor remembers which road flooded last winter.
help: Organize practical warnings without announcing the banjo as an oracle
helpOutcome: A volunteer closes the vulnerable road. The band moves indoors. Nobody asks the banjo to sign the incident report.

title: A Community Potluck for Cryptids
premise: A potluck has a strict no-photography policy and suspiciously good pie.
pressure: The cryptid potluck has three rules: bring a dish, label the ingredients, and take no photographs. A neighbor has arrived with a telephoto lens because he thinks privacy is what guilty people ask for. Someone inside is serving extraordinary rhubarb pie.
investigate: Ask the hosts why they refuse photographs, without barging into their gathering
success: The hosts explain that their guests move between wildlife corridors the camera club keeps exposing. Their seating plan marks routes the county should protect, not a location to upload.
failure: The lens flashes despite your request. Several guests slip away. The neighbor deletes the image when he realizes he has frightened people who were only eating dinner.
help: Put away your phone, label your dish and respect the invitation's boundaries
helpOutcome: Everyone who wants a slice gets one. The neighbor leaves the camera in the car and discovers the pie does not require a confession.

title: The Airport of Unscheduled Arrivals
premise: An aircraft lands with no engine noise and excellent snacks.
pressure: A silent plane lands at Kneeland and presents a passenger manifest full of people not yet born. The pilot hands out excellent sandwiches. Ground crew worry about fuel, headcount and a runway occupied by a craft nobody cleared to land.
investigate: Check the aircraft registration and manifest against the runway log without boarding
success: The registration corresponds to a flight booked for next spring. Ground control records the discrepancy and keeps the runway closed until the plane is inspected.
failure: The manifest pages turn blank in the wind. A mechanic still records the unusual landing marks and the crew's exact arrival time.
help: Help ground staff keep the passengers safe and clear the approach
helpOutcome: Everyone waits in a sheltered area while the airfield radios for advice. The pilot's sandwiches are the least controversial item on the incident report.

title: The Amateur UFO Tow Truck
premise: Two neighbors offer roadside service for saucers stuck in mud.
pressure: Two neighbors operate a UFO tow service from a pickup older than most of its parts. Their latest customer has buried a saucer in Kneeland mud. The pilot barely reaches the warning triangle; the tow operator is already promising to pull it out before the cable is rated.
investigate: Check the recovery points and load before anyone stands near the tow line
success: The metal shavings lead toward a relay antenna the county says is not yet installed. You bag a sample and leave the vehicle alone until the crew declares the scene safe.
failure: The first line snaps under a test load, far from the onlookers. The pilot provides a better drawing of the craft and admits it has no approved tow hook.
help: Organize a slower extraction with boards, a spotter and room for the pilot to refuse
helpOutcome: The crew builds a stable path and eases the craft free without a heroic jerk on the cable. The grateful pilot offers tomorrow's weather and no explanation for the saucer.

title: The Fog That Followed You Home
premise: A personal patch of fog is politely but relentlessly attached.
pressure: Your own personal fog follows you into a grocery store, joins the checkout queue and makes the scanner display prices from twenty years ago. The cashier is being blamed for a sale they cannot control; a shopper is struggling to find the exit through the mist.
investigate: Test the fog's boundary with the store's ventilation and compare the scanner receipts
success: The patch drifts toward a receipt dated on the same missing Tuesday as an earlier clue. The cashier keeps a copy; the store's prices remain today's.
failure: The fog changes shape faster than you can measure it. You save the itemized receipt and the cashier notes which aisle first clouded.
help: Help the shopper reach the door and let staff decide whether to evacuate
helpOutcome: The exit clears and the cashier gets backup instead of blame. The fog leaves with a loyalty card nobody remembers issuing.

title: The Midnight Cattle Crossing
premise: Cows follow invisible traffic signals with military precision.
pressure: Cattle are obeying invisible traffic signals on a narrow backroad. A delivery van is edging toward the herd while its driver assumes the cows are being stubborn. The rancher says they are the most punctual animals on the property.
investigate: Compare the herd's stopping points with the bend in the road and recorded traffic
success: The invisible 'green' falls exactly when the blind curve is clear. The rancher marks the crossing and requests a real caution sign.
failure: A passing truck scatters the herd before you can time it. Your dash-camera still catches the cows waiting at the same patch of pavement.
help: Help slow the vehicles and give the rancher room to move the cattle safely
helpOutcome: The herd crosses without incident. A cow pauses beside your car until you apologize for honking; the rancher says she does that to everyone.

title: Antenna for the Wrong Stars
premise: A ham-radio operator catches weather reports from an unfamiliar constellation.
pressure: A ham-radio operator receives a weather bulletin for stars no telescope can locate, followed by tomorrow's wind warning for Kneeland. A neighbor is preparing for a ridge-top job and needs a reliable forecast, not a lesson in celestial bureaucracy.
investigate: Record the transmission and compare the local forecast with independent weather readings
success: The unfamiliar call sign overlays a legitimate storm pressure trend. The operator shares the recording while the neighbor checks an ordinary weather service.
failure: Static swallows the coordinates before a second receiver locks on. You keep the transmission time and a repeatable fragment of the call sign.
help: Help the neighbor make a conservative plan for the ridge-top work
helpOutcome: The crew reschedules exposed tasks and the radio operator keeps listening from home. The stars are invited to file future reports in local units.

title: Bigfoot's Custody Weekend
premise: Two Sasquatch parents ask the player to mediate a family logistics argument.
pressure: Two Sasquatch parents are arguing over a muddy backpack, not over their child. The child has been spending weekends in both homes and wants everyone to stop changing the pickup time. Their neighbor has arrived with a camera because somebody promised a television special.
investigate: Ask the child which arrangements work and let the adults check the details
success: The child's crayon map identifies a sheltered route and a familiar tree where pickups can happen without cameras. The adults agree to try it before debating whose idea it was.
failure: The argument gets loud and the child leaves the clearing. You stop the discussion until both parents find them together and ask what would help.
help: Help the parents write a handoff plan the child can actually follow
helpOutcome: The parents settle on one familiar meeting tree and a backup rainy-day location. The neighbor goes home without photographs or a custody exclusive.

title: The Museum's Escaped Footprint
premise: A plaster cast takes a midnight walk and leaves fresh tracks.
pressure: A plaster footprint has walked out of its museum case, leaving wet tracks through the parking lot. The curator is expected to report a missing artifact before opening and fears the donors will be told she sold it.
investigate: Compare the case inventory and the tracks without walking over the evidence
success: The wet tracks stop at the old loading dock; an accession photo shows the cast positioned differently last night. The curator logs both facts.
failure: A cleaning truck crosses the last print. A security guard has already sketched its shape and notes the time it appeared.
help: Help the curator secure the gallery and report the incident accurately
helpOutcome: The museum stays open with a temporary label explaining the missing cast. The donors receive a plain account, which offends only the ghost of public relations.

title: The Other Bigfoot Research Society
premise: Researchers have conclusive proof of tinyfeet and are furious nobody cares.
pressure: The Other Bigfoot Research Society presents decades of careful evidence for tiny humanlike footprints. Their grant was cut after a television crew insisted they change the poster to BIGFOOT, and their youngest researcher has stopped bringing findings to meetings.
investigate: Check the casts against the field notes without promising a sensational conclusion
success: One cast's tread pattern matches a trail marker that was installed next year, according to the date on the team's survey. The evidence is intriguing; the researcher wants another independent measurement.
failure: A fragile cast breaks under the examination light. The field notebooks survive, and you help the team write down exactly what was damaged.
help: Give the youngest researcher time to explain the work in their own words
helpOutcome: The society books a modest library presentation with labeled uncertainties and no mascot. The researcher volunteers to speak again.

title: The River Claims a Witness
premise: A message in driftwood names a witness who was never present.
pressure: Driftwood spells the name of a witness who insists she has never stood on this riverbank. A neighbor has already started accusing her of hiding something. She wants the board removed before the rumor reaches her workplace.
investigate: Check the lettering against flood marks and ask the named person what, if anything, she consents to share
success: A current scar runs under the carved letters; the timing is strange, not a confession. You document the wood without adding a theory about her life.
failure: The water pulls the board away before you measure it. The witness keeps a photograph, and you can corroborate the rising-water time.
help: Help stop the rumor and get the witness safely away from the bank
helpOutcome: The neighbor retracts the accusation and the witness goes home. The river offers no apology, but it does stop spelling names for an hour.

title: A Cryptid's Online Dating Profile
premise: A woodland resident wants help writing a bio with less obvious fur-related clues.
pressure: A shy, very large forest resident needs help with a dating profile. Every draft lists exact footprints, fur density and the location of its den. A well-meaning friend keeps insisting a viral reveal would make the perfect first impression.
investigate: Ask which details belong in a bio and which would put the resident at risk
success: A draft built around interests, humor and boundaries attracts a thoughtful reply without exposing the den. The resident chooses whether to answer.
failure: The photo upload fails and the friend posts an accidental silhouette. You remove identifying tags before it spreads and document what was shared.
help: Help write a profile that gives the resident control over disclosure
helpOutcome: The bio opens with a terrible mushroom joke and a genuine question about music. The den stays private; the friend agrees not to do publicity.

title: Mile Marker Zero and a Half
premise: A roadside sign changes distance whenever somebody lies.
pressure: On Highway 299, a mile marker advances every time somebody on the bus tells a lie. The driver has lost two miles on tonight's route and has a wheelchair passenger who must make a connection. The other riders begin demanding confessions from strangers.
investigate: Compare the changing sign with odometer readings and fixed landmarks
success: The distance changes only on the roadside sign, not the actual junctions. An unmarked detour appears on the bus map and you note which version was posted first.
failure: Someone jokes and the number jumps again. You cannot prove the rule, but the driver records a reliable turnoff beyond the next bend.
help: Stop the interrogation and coordinate a route that gets everyone to their stops
helpOutcome: Passengers call ahead, the driver uses known landmarks, and the connection is held. Nobody is required to reveal a private lie to earn a ride.

title: The Hitchhiker Who Hitches Time
premise: A polite rider pays in gas receipts dated ten years ahead.
pressure: A polite hitchhiker offers receipts for fuel not sold until a decade from now. He knows the exit you planned to take but will not say how. The road is dark and another driver has already pulled over in an unsafe turnoff.
investigate: Check the receipt's station number and future price without taking the stranger anywhere
success: The business number belongs to a station not yet opened. You record it from a safe turnout and leave the man's story unverified.
failure: The ink smears before you can read the address. A printed transaction code remains, enough to compare with public records later.
help: Help the stranded rider contact safe transport without promising a lift
helpOutcome: A local shuttle confirms a pickup at a lit stop. The traveler waits with a thermos and refuses to explain why tomorrow's fuel is so expensive.

title: The Last Working Pay Phone
premise: An empty booth rings with calls from missing county offices.
pressure: The last pay phone on Highway 299 rings outside a shuttered store. Every caller claims to work at a county office that was never built. One wants a document retrieved urgently; another sounds frightened and simply wants somebody to answer.
investigate: Write down the call signs and cross-check them with publicly listed offices
success: Three callers identify the same records room at different future dates. A current clerk confirms the street address exists, but no such room has been approved.
failure: The line cuts off before the caller gives an address. The handset displays an incomplete number and a retired clerk recognizes its old exchange.
help: Help the frightened caller reach a staffed service without promising a miracle
helpOutcome: A retired clerk helps connect a living caller to the right present-day desk. The phone continues ringing, but at least one person gets an answer.

title: The Alien Rest Area Review
premise: Visitors from elsewhere leave harsh customer-service ratings for Earth.
pressure: Visitors from another planet have posted a one-star review of a highway rest stop, citing gravity, plumbing and the difficulty of finding a vegetarian snack. The caretaker fears a poor public rating will cost their tiny maintenance budget.
investigate: Read the reviews against the site's actual safety and accessibility report
success: Beneath the nonsense is a correct note about a faulty tap. The caretaker files a repair request with an earthly ticket number.
failure: The aliens delete the most specific post. A paper inspection checklist still records the same leak and the date it began.
help: Help the caretaker address the real problem and answer the complaints without ridicule
helpOutcome: The tap gets a temporary out-of-order sign and the visitors receive directions to a safer stop. Their revised review awards Earth two stars for effort.

title: The Logging Road to the Backroom
premise: A dirt road branches into a warehouse storing abandoned dreams.
pressure: A logging road leads to a warehouse full of boxed dreams, each tagged with a name and an uncollected claim ticket. An older worker recognizes a box from his childhood and asks not to have its contents opened in front of strangers.
investigate: Examine the ledger and the warehouse's land-use records before touching any box
success: The inventory lists a pickup date that has not arrived. The worker gets a copy of his entry and keeps control of whether to claim it.
failure: A shelf collapses before you can match the lot numbers. You rescue a page showing where the missing boxes were stored, without opening them.
help: Help secure the unstable shelves and protect the workers' privacy
helpOutcome: The building is closed until its racks are safe. The worker leaves with an unbroken claim ticket and the choice of returning someday.
